First read /tmp/AGENT_GUIDE.md carefully (rules + engine API). You work in a git worktree of /workspace (build with `cargo build --release` in your worktree root).

YOUR TASK: implement `Intl` to match the ORIGINAL binary. You own `src/builtins/intl.rs` (current draft is minimal; rewrite freely, possibly splitting into new files under `src/builtins/intl/` as a directory module — keep the public functions other code uses: `intl::setup(vm)`, `intl::number_to_locale_string(vm, x, &locales, &options)`, `intl::group_digits_str(s, sep)`, `intl::locale_list(vm, &v)`, `intl::read_dtf_options(vm, &v)`, `intl::throw_dt_error(vm, e)`). DateTimeFormat formatting already exists in `src/datetime.rs` (a very complete, verified implementation of the original's date formatting incl. locales/options/time zones — READ its top doc comment); wire Intl.DateTimeFormat fully to it (format getter bound function, formatToParts, formatRange/formatRangeToParts if the original has them, resolvedOptions with exact key order, supportedLocalesOf, error messages).

Probe the original for: `Object.getOwnPropertyNames(Intl)` = getCanonicalLocales,supportedValuesOf,Locale,ListFormat,PluralRules,RelativeTimeFormat,NumberFormat,Collator,DisplayNames,Segmenter,DurationFormat,DateTimeFormat. For EACH: constructor behavior, option validation and exact error messages, resolvedOptions (key order!), formatting outputs across locales (the original has a small built-in locale table — e.g. NumberFormat: en "1,234,567.891", de-DE "1.234.567,891", en-IN "12,34,567.891", fr-FR "1 234 567,891" with U+202F; currency en-US EUR "€1,234.50", de-DE "1.234,50 €", ja-JP JPY "¥1,235"; compact "1.2M"; unit "12 km"; percent), formatToParts, signDisplay, notation (scientific/engineering/compact short/long), rounding options, useGrouping, min/max digits, BigInt formatting; Number.prototype.toLocaleString & BigInt.prototype.toLocaleString & Array/Date toLocaleString integration; PluralRules (select, selectRange, resolvedOptions; note the original's ordinal rules may be incomplete — e.g. `new Intl.PluralRules('en',{type:'ordinal'}).select(2)` gives "other"); ListFormat (types/styles/locales, formatToParts); RelativeTimeFormat (numeric auto/always, styles, units incl. plural forms, formatToParts); Collator (compare with sensitivity/numeric/caseFirst/ignorePunctuation; sort order of mixed-case/accents — String.prototype.localeCompare is implemented in src/builtins/string.rs `locale_cmp`; you may improve that function too (you're allowed to edit only that function there) so both agree with the original); Segmenter (grapheme/word/sentence segmentation with isWordLike, containing()); DisplayNames (languages/regions/scripts/currencies for a few locales); Locale (properties, maximize/minimize, toString, getters like hourCycles/calendars...); DurationFormat (format/formatToParts styles); getCanonicalLocales/supportedValuesOf outputs.

Write comparison scripts in /tmp/intlagent/ and iterate until outputs match the original byte-for-byte (focus first on what typical test programs would use: toLocaleString defaults, NumberFormat currency/percent/compact, PluralRules, ListFormat, RelativeTimeFormat, Collator, DateTimeFormat). Commit in your worktree branch. Final reply: branch/commit, what's done, known differences, core-engine bugs found (with JS repro).

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

content.content:
# Guide for subagents working on the lumen reimplementation

## The project
We are reimplementing, from scratch in Rust (std only, NO external crates), a JavaScript engine +
Node/Bun-like runtime called "lumen" (CLI `lumen-cli`). The ORIGINAL compiled binary is at
`/workspace/executable` (symlink `/tmp/orig`). Our reimplementation lives in the git repo `/workspace`
(you will be working in your own git worktree copy of it). Hidden tests will run JS programs through
both binaries and compare stdout, stderr and exit code EXACTLY, so fidelity to the original's
observable behavior (output formats, error messages, property orders, edge cases) is the goal.

## Rules (strict)
- You may RUN the original (`/tmp/orig file.js`, `/tmp/orig -e 'code'`) to observe behavior.
- You MUST NOT disassemble/decompile/read the original binary's bytes, use strace/ltrace/gdb on it,
  search the internet, or download anything. No network is available anyway.
- Do not copy JS source code text of the original's internal modules verbatim (some functions print
  their JS source via `String(fn)`; you may observe *behavior*, but write your own Rust implementation).
- Write Rust (std only). Keep any scratch scripts (shell/python/JS test files) OUTSIDE the repo, e.g.
  under `/tmp/<yourname>/`. Do not add non-Rust code files to the repo.
- Only edit the files assigned to you. If a core-engine bug blocks you, work around it in your files
  if possible and describe the bug precisely in your final report (file/function, repro JS). If you
  absolutely must touch a shared file, keep the change minimal and list it in your report.
- Never run `/workspace/compile.sh` and never write to `/workspace/executable`.
- Build with `cargo build --release` in YOUR worktree (binary: `target/release/lumen`). Commit your
  work in your worktree with clear messages when done (and at milestones).
- `console.log` in lumen prints values via `String(v)` (objects print as `[object Object]`), so when
  probing the original use JSON.stringify or explicit string building.

## Engine architecture (what you need to write builtins)
Key modules (in `src/`): `value.rs` (Value, JsStr, Sym, PropKey), `object.rs` (Obj, ObjKind, Prop,
PropDesc, Args, NativeFn, flags WRITABLE/ENUMERABLE/CONFIGURABLE, WEC, WC), `vm.rs` (Vm, JsResult,
calls, errors, frames, Job), `props.rs` (property internal methods on Vm), `ops.rs` (conversions),
`realm.rs` (intrinsics + helpers to define builtins), `builtins/*` (ECMAScript builtins),
`runtime/*` (node/web runtime), `runtime/mod.rs` (Host state, event loop), `modules.rs` (ESM).

### Values
```rust
enum Value { Undefined, Null, Bool(bool), Num(f64), Str(JsStr), Sym(Sym), BigInt(Rc<BigInt>), Obj(Obj), Empty /*internal*/ }
JsStr::from_str("x"), s.to_rust_string(), s.units() -> &[u16] (UTF-16), JsStr::from_units(vec), JsStr::concat(&a,&b)
Value::str("x"), Value::Num(1.0), v.is_undefined(), v.is_nullish(), v.as_obj() -> Option<&Obj>, v.truthy(), v.is_callable()
PropKey::from_str("name"), PropKey::Str(js), PropKey::Sym(sym), PropKey::from_index(i)
```
### Natives
```rust
type NativeFn = fn(&mut Vm, &Args) -> JsResult<Value>;   // JsResult<T> = Result<T, Value /*thrown*/>
// Args: a.this (Value), a.args (&[Value]), a.arg(i) -> Value (undefined if missing), a.callee (&Obj),
//       a.new_target (Option<Obj>, Some when called with `new`), a.slot(i) -> captured data (see native_closure)
vm.native_fn("name", length, f) -> Obj                         // function object
vm.native_closure("name", length, f, vec![slot0, slot1]) -> Obj // with captured Values (read via a.slot(i))
vm.def_method(&obj, "name", length, f) -> Obj                    // non-enumerable writable configurable method
vm.def_getter(&obj, "name", f); vm.def_accessor(&obj, "name", getter, setter)
vm.native_ctor("Name", length, f, &proto) -> Obj   // constructor; links proto.constructor & ctor.prototype
// In a constructor native: let p = vm.proto_from_nt(&a.new_target, &fallback_proto)?; Obj::new(Some(p), kind)
vm.make_ctor(&fobj)  // mark a native fn as constructible
vm.def_global("Name", Value::Obj(o)); vm.set_tag(&obj, "Tag") // Symbol.toStringTag
```
### Objects
```rust
vm.new_object() -> Obj (plain, Object.prototype); vm.obj_from(vec![("k", v), ...]) -> Obj (enumerable props)
vm.new_array(vec![...]) -> Obj; Obj::new(proto: Option<Obj>, ObjKind::Ordinary)
o.set_str("k", v, WEC); o.set_prop(PropKey, v, flags); o.get_own_str("k") -> Option<Value> (own data only)
o.borrow() / o.borrow_mut()  (RefCell — never hold a borrow across a call into JS!)
// custom native state: Obj::new(Some(proto), ObjKind::Host(Box::new(MyState{..}))) and later
//   if let ObjKind::Host(h) = &o.borrow().kind { if let Some(s) = h.downcast_ref::<MyState>() {..} }
//   (use Cell/RefCell inside MyState for mutation)
crate::runtime::reorder_enum(vm, &obj, &["a","b",...]) // force enumerable key order (missing -> noop fns)
```
### Property access / conversions (all on `vm`)
```rust
vm.get(&obj, &key, &receiver_value)?; vm.get_str(&obj, "name")?; vm.get_prop_of(&value, &key)? (works on primitives)
vm.set_prop_of(&value, key, v, /*strict*/ true)?; vm.create_data_property(&obj, key, v)?
vm.has_property(&obj, &key)?; vm.delete(&obj, &key)?; vm.own_property_keys(&obj)?; vm.enumerable_own_keys(&obj)?
vm.to_string(&v)? -> JsStr; vm.to_number(&v)?; vm.to_object(&v)?; vm.to_property_key(&v)?; vm.to_index(&v)?
vm.to_integer_or_infinity(&v)?; vm.to_int32/to_uint32; vm.to_primitive(&v, crate::ops::Hint::Default)?
crate::runtime::display_value(vm, &v) -> String   // what console.log prints for a value
crate::runtime::util::inspect_value(vm, &v, depth)? -> String  // util.inspect
crate::runtime::util::describe_received(vm, &v) -> String // Node-style "Received type number (5)"
vm.call(&f, this, &args)?; vm.construct(&ctor, &args, None)?; vm.iterate_to_vec(&iterable)?
crate::builtins::array::array_like_to_vec(vm, &v)?
```
### Errors
```rust
return vm.throw_type("message");   // also throw_range, throw_ref, throw_syntax, throw_error("URIError", msg)
let e = vm.make_error("TypeError", "msg"); if let Value::Obj(o) = &e { o.set_prop(PropKey::from_str("code"), Value::str("ERR_X"), WEC); } return Err(e);
```
### Promises / async / event loop
```rust
let cap = vm.new_promise_capability_intrinsic(); // Capability { promise, resolve, reject }
vm.call(&cap.resolve, Value::Undefined, &[v])?; return Ok(cap.promise);
crate::builtins::promise::promise_then(vm, &promise_obj, on_fulfilled_fn_value, on_rejected_fn_value)?
crate::builtins::promise::perform_then_internal(vm, &p, Handler::Native(f, data), Handler::Native(g, data), None)
   // f: fn(&mut Vm, Value /*result*/, &Value /*data*/) -> JsResult<Value>
vm.jobs.push_back(crate::vm::Job::Callback(f, args));      // microtask
vm.host.callbacks.push_back((f, args));                     // macrotask (setImmediate-like queue)
crate::runtime::timers::add_timer(vm, cb, delay_ms, args, repeat) -> id
crate::runtime::spawn_op(vm, move || { /* runs on a thread, return T: Send */ }, move |vm, t: T| { /* back on loop thread */ });
   // keeps the event loop alive until `then` runs. Never move Values/Objs into the thread closure.
```
### Buffers / bytes
```rust
crate::runtime::buffer::new_buffer_value(vm, bytes)?      // Node Buffer (Uint8Array subclass)
crate::runtime::buffer::bytes_of(vm, &v)?                  // bytes of string(utf8)/Buffer/TypedArray/ArrayBuffer/array
crate::builtins::typedarray::ta_bytes(&obj)                // bytes of TypedArray/ArrayBuffer/DataView
crate::builtins::typedarray::typed_array_from_bytes(vm, bytes) -> Obj  // plain Uint8Array
crate::runtime::buffer::{encode_string, decode_bytes, norm_encoding}   // node encodings
crate::runtime::encoding::{base64_encode, base64_decode_strict, hex_encode, utf16_to_utf8, utf8_to_utf16}
```
### EventEmitter helpers
`crate::runtime::events::{install_methods(vm,&proto), init_emitter(vm,&obj), emit_event(vm,&this_value,&Value::str("evt"),&args)?}`
and `create_module(vm)` returns the EventEmitter constructor (also cached via `crate::runtime::node::builtin_module(vm, "events")?`).

### Module registry
`crate::runtime::node::builtin_module(vm, "name")? -> Option<Value>` returns (cached) exports of a node
builtin (used by `require`, `import`, `process.getBuiltinModule`). The dispatch is in
`runtime/node.rs::builtin_module`; your module's `create_module(vm, name)` is already wired.
Globals are installed by `setup(vm)` functions called from `runtime/mod.rs::setup_runtime`.

## Testing
Write JS test files under `/tmp/<yourname>/` and compare outputs of `/tmp/orig` vs your build:
`/tmp/orig t.js > o1 2> e1; echo $? ; target/release/lumen t.js > o2 2> e2; echo $?; diff o1 o2; diff e1 e2`.
Cover typical usage first (what a test-writer would exercise), then edge cases and error messages.
Note process.argv[0]/timings legitimately differ.

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

import unicodedata, sys
lines = [l for l in open('/tmp/intlagent/coll/dump_bmp.txt').read().split('\n') if l]
seq = []
for l in lines:
    cp, _, rel = l.partition(' ')
    seq.append((int(cp, 16), rel))

def nfd(c):
    return unicodedata.normalize('NFD', c)

def lower(ch):
    l = ch.lower()
    return l

def hyp_key(cp):
    c = chr(cp)
    d = nfd(c)
    prim = []
    sec = []
    ter = []
    for ch in d:
        if unicodedata.combining(ch) != 0 and prim:
            sec[-1].append(ord(ch))
            continue
        l = ch.lower()
        prim.append(tuple(ord(x) for x in l))
        sec.append([])
        ter.append(1 if ch != l else 0)
    return prim, sec, ter

# check primary order: consecutive elements must have nondecreasing primary in hypothesis, and equality iff rel[0]=='='
bad = 0
prev = None
for i, (cp, rel) in enumerate(seq):
    k = hyp_key(cp)
    if prev is not None:
        pk = prev[1]
        exp_eq = (pk[0] == k[0])
        got_eq = rel[0] == '='
        lt = pk[0] < k[0]
        if got_eq != exp_eq or (not got_eq and not lt):
            bad += 1
            if bad < 60:
                print('mismatch', hex(prev[0]), repr(chr(prev[0])), hex(cp), repr(chr(cp)), rel, pk[0], k[0])
    prev = (cp, k)
print('bad', bad, 'of', len(seq))

Intl.Collator and String.prototype.localeCompare are done and match the original. The only remaining differences come from two things outside my files.

**Branch / commit:** `worktree-agent-a7a64ea381028e8a0` @ `0b8098b` (based on your skeleton `259405d`).

**Files changed:**
- `src/builtins/intl/collator.rs`: full rewrite (constructor, `resolvedOptions`, `compare` getter and the collation algorithm).
- `src/builtins/string.rs`: only `locale_cmp` and `locale_compare` changed. `localeCompare` now goes through the collator; `pub fn locale_cmp(a, b, sens)` is kept as a wrapper.
- `intl/mod.rs` is untouched.

**How the original sorts (it is not CLDR):**
- **Primary:** each character is decomposed (NFD) and lowercased, then compared by code point. Nothing is ignorable, `_` sorts after `@`, and ß, æ, Greek and Cyrillic sort after z.
- **Accents:** each base character counts as 0 and each combining mark as its code point, compared as one flat sequence.
- **Case:** an "is uppercase" flag per base character; titlecase digraphs like ǅ count as lowercase.
- There is no identical level, so canonically equivalent strings compare equal. Results are always -1/0/1.
- Accent order is primary then accents; case order is primary then case; variant is all three.
- **numeric:** only ASCII digit runs count, compared by value. Leading zeros show up at the accent and case levels because each digit adds an entry there.
- **ignorePunctuation:** drops ASCII punctuation/symbols, whitespace and U+2000–U+206F after decomposition. It defaults to true for `th`.
- **caseFirst upper** puts uppercase first.
- **German phonebook or `usage: 'search'`:** ä/ö/ü expand to ae/oe/ue with an accent difference. No other locale has any tailoring (sv, es and the rest sort like en).
- **Settings:**
  - Option read order, error messages, `-u-co/kf/kn` handling (including the original's quirks) and which collations each language supports all match.
  - Internal `__co_*` slots are read on every call, and the brand is checked again inside the bound compare.
  - `__co_bound` is returned as-is whenever it exists.

**Verification:**
- All BMP code points and a sample across all planes, at all four sensitivities, give byte-identical output.
- About 400k random string pairs over 256 option combinations match, as do 18 probe scripts and typical name, file and number sorts.
- It is faster than the original (a 50k-word sort takes about 1.4s versus 8–9s).

**Remaining differences, both outside my files:**
1. Bug in your `locale_list` in `mod.rs`: `null` locales should throw `TypeError: Cannot convert null to object`. It currently gives the engine's `cannot convert undefined or null to object`. Repro: `new Intl.Collator(null)`, `Intl.getCanonicalLocales(null)`, `'a'.localeCompare('b', null)`. The fix is one line: `Value::Null => return vm.throw_type("Cannot convert null to object")`.
2. `'ä'.localeCompare('ae', new Intl.Locale(...))` fails only because `Intl.Locale` is still a stub.

**Applies to your DateTimeFormat/NumberFormat getters:**
- If the cached bound slot exists, the original returns it even when it is `undefined`. Repro: `d = new Intl.DateTimeFormat(); d.__dtf_bound = undefined; typeof d.format` gives `"undefined"`, and the same happens with `__nf_boundformat`. Your getters treat `undefined` as missing.
- For Collator, the bound function re-checks the brand before converting its arguments: `f = c.compare; delete c.__co; f('a','b')` throws "method called on an incompatible receiver". I did not test whether `format` does the same.
